titulo_es: The present congiuntive: forms and opinions

congiuntivo.consejo: Verbal mode of doubt, opinion and subjectivity.

credere.consejo: The word of opinion that governs congiuntive.

dubitare.consejo: The word of doubt that governs congiuntive.

texto: In the verbs in **-are**, the subjunctive present ends in **-i** for io, you, lui / lei: **parli, parli, parli**. In the verbs in **-ere** and **-ire** ends in **-a**: **prenda, dorma, finisca**.
Key irregular forms: **essere → sia**, **avere → abbia**, **andare → vada**, **venire → venga**, **fare → faccia**, **sapere → sappia**.

With verbs of opinion: **Penso che sia vero** (I think it's true), **Credo che abbia ragione** (I think it's right). With a doubt or wish: **Spero che tu venga** (I hope you will come), **Non sono sicuro che parta** (I'm not sure it will come out).

frases.it: Non credo che sia troppo duro. Ma bisogna che si studi.
frases.es: No creo que sea demasiado duro. Pero hace falta que se estudie.
frases.en: I don't think it's too hard. But it needs to be studied.
You'll see how it's going to go well!

bloques.pregunta: What verbal mode does «penso che» or «credo che» usually follow in formal Italian?

opciones.explicacion: The verbs of subjective judgment or unsure opinion govern congiuntive.
It is used for hypothesis or courtesy, not as a basic regime after «penso che».
The imperative expresses direct orders or pleas.

bloques.pregunta: What is the present congiuntive form of «essere» for «lui»?

opciones.explicacion: The three people of the singular share the «sia» form (ia sia, your sia, lui sia).
«È» is the form of an indicative present: a safe fact.
«Fosse» is an imfetus congiuntive.

bloques.frase: Spero che Marco ___ presto alla festa.

opciones.explicacion: Congiuntive present irregular verb «venire».
It is present as an indication («He's coming.»).
It's congiuntive imfetus.

opciones.texto: A sincere desire for the other person to come soon.
opciones.explicacion: «Sperare che» rules congiuntive to manifest desire.

opciones.texto: An absolute certainty that the person has already arrived.
opciones.explicacion: It does not claim a certain fact but an expectation.

opciones.texto: A clear order that forbids the appointment.
opciones.explicacion: It is not a ban but a kind hope.

opciones.texto: Porque expresa una opinión personal subjetiva introducida por «penso che».
opciones.explicacion: The verb «pensare» directs the subordinate to the congiuntive.

opciones.texto: Porque describe una verdad matemática demostrada e incuestionable.
opciones.explicacion: The objective certainty would require indicative with «so che».

opciones.texto: Because the subject is plural of courtesy.
opciones.explicacion: The grammar subject of the subordinate is singular.

bloques.frase: Credo che Marco abbia ragione su questo punto
bloques.traduccion: I think Marco is right at this point.
bloques.explicacion: Opinion prayer with «credere che» and present congiuntive «avere».

bloques.pregunta: How do you say in Italian «I hope it's true.»?

opciones.explicacion: «Sperare che» + present congiuntive of essere («sia»).
The «è» sign is disadvised in the formal standard record.
«Fosse» transfers the desire to the congiuntive imfetus.

bloques.frase: Non credo che loro ___ già la risposta corretta.

opciones.explicacion: Third person of plural of the present congiuntive of «sapere».
It is present as an indication: «They know.».
It's congiuntive imfect plural.

intro: The congiuntive is used for opinions, doubts, desires and things that are not safe. In Spanish it is the subjunctive («I think it's / it's easy»). It is very common with verbs as I will think, believe and sperare.
